messages.subject: weird shapes in poppr_msn
parts:
Dear all, 

I am trying to build minimum spanning networks for RADseq SNP data, with ~20.000 SNPs.
Following the "primer in population genomics, part III", I use a genlight object, calculate genetic distance between individuals using bitwise.dist() and then create network using poppr.msn(). 
As expected with large SNP datasets, each node represents a single individual. However, the the shape of my networks are weird and I think they do not represent well my data.  I get a sort of starlike shape: 1 individual in the center and all individuals (from different populations, including individuals from the same population as the central individual) spanning from it, at the same distance. In other analyses, e.g. PCA, Structure, I've seen that there is population structure, which does not correspond to this shape of MSN. I have work with MSN before and kind of understand when to expect a star-like shape, but this is not the case. 

I don't know what I'm doing wrong, or if there is a problem applying this method to my kind of data. 

Thanks a lot in advance for your help, 

All the best

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] weird shapes in poppr_msn
parts:
Hello,

I'm not sure if you are doing anything wrong per se. The minimum spanning network is constructed from the distance matrix between all individuals using Prim's algorithm, so what you get is a representation of minimum set of edges needed to connect all the nodes in your network. My guess (and only a guess) is that while you have apparent population structure, there is still a lot of variation within groups that's strong enough to overpower the MSN. One thing you could try if you haven't already is to add the parameter include.ties = TRUE to see if you have equivalent paths. You might also consider using a Euclidean distance (use the option euclidean = TRUE and scale_missing = TRUE in bitwise.dist), which will differentiate between homozygous and heterozygous sites. You might also consider taking a look at what the tree from bitwise.dist looks like. I would suspect it has a lot of long terminal branches without strong boostrap support.

That being said, I could be completely off the mark here.

I hope that helps,
Zhian
